t: This is the British Institute for the Study of Iraq, the only body in Britain devoted to research into the ancient civilisations and languages of Mesopotamia. It was founded in 1932 to support research into the archaeology of Iraq and neighbouring countries, from the earliest times to around 1700 AD, and to promote Iraq's cultural heritage. It publishes the annual journal Iraq. It carries the name of Gertrude Bell, the traveller, writer and archaeologist who spent much of her life exploring and mapping the Middle East. British officials trusted her, and she took part in the 1921 Cairo Conference on the region's future.
